original_card.question: Is there meaningful uncovered packing headroom for an exact current word and boundary contract?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live overlap and exact model/source binding first. Distinguish a chronological construction from a pooled optimum. State the applicable fixed-inventory ceiling and remaining headroom; changed words or interfaces require a new fully charged model. Do not launch a residual search without an explicit scope and time cap.

Require an unclaimed domain, time cap and useful complete margin. Stop at the applicable ceiling; change the word or boundary instead of adding seeds.

actual_scope: Chart-assignment headroom of the exact PR6030 local P104 word (and, for comparison, the PR5907 and PR5827 words): edits that keep the scalar program's events and change only frames, MOVEs or commuting event timing, priced by PR5827 local.py's paid-rank rule and replayed by its unmodified replay.
scope_change_reason: The fixed-invoice packing ceiling of PR6030 is already its raw crossing (PROOF-REVIEW.md), so the next packing question is whether the paid profile itself has slack that needs no scalar rewrite. This tests the one degree of freedom that the paid rank rule exposes: which chart each register occupies when.
bottleneck_link: Complex binds the selected outer assembly (main_transform). Each complex step since PR5811 changed the local paid profile; this shows that, for the PR6030 word, such a step cannot come from re-charting or retiming alone in the four tested classes and must change the scalar program (as PR5827, PR5907 and PR6030 did).
stop_rule: Stop at one exhaustive pass of each class over the three words with positive controls; any positive proposal would be handed to the full PR5827 chain rather than claimed.
evidence: verify.py: classes A-E on PR6030/PR5907/PR5827 words, zero positive proposals; three synthetic controls on PR6030 (inserted unread rung found by A-D; worsened meeting chart found by B, C and E; rung holding two SCALEs found by A and B), every class A proposal and every positive class B proposal replayed by PR5827 local.py, class E priced by the nesting rule. RESULT.json is regenerated and compared byte for byte.

open_questions.question: Can read rerouting (a register reading a source directly instead of through an intermediate register, as in PR6030 where helper 268 reads 2*704 at frame 714 and helper 560 no longer reads 704 at frame 612) be searched systematically, and does it expose stays that classes A-E can then delete?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All three recent complex steps were of this shape; this package shows chart edits alone are exhausted, so the scalar rewrite is the step that creates headroom.
open_questions.first_step: Using the exact row replay of PR5827 local.py, list every ADD d += q*k whose source k carries a single-source term that k receives at a frame d never visits; test whether d can take that term directly at a frame it shares with the source, then rerun classes A-E on the rewritten word.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a rewrite engine that keeps every row identity; PR5827 local.py can serve as the exact checker.

open_questions.question: Do re-charts of three or more linked meetings, or of linked pairs over arbitrary (unlisted) subspaces, find a gain that classes C and E miss?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Class C is coordinate-wise and class E covers pairs over listed frames only; a concave rank cost can reward larger joint moves.
open_questions.first_step: Extend class E to arbitrary subspaces between the pair's outer bounds, then to chains of three meetings.
open_questions.blocked_by: None; it is a bounded extension of class C.
